bib.title: A Comprehensive Capability Analysis of GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 Series Models

read.skipped: Reference list only skimmed. Every results table (2-24) and every prompt table (25-45) was read; the long English passages in the SQuAD prompt tables are one fixed Notre Dame passage repeated.

question: How do the NLU capabilities and robustness of GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 series models change as OpenAI's training strategies evolve?
contributions: Zero-shot, 1-shot and 3-shot evaluation of six GPT-series models on 9 NLU tasks / 21 datasets plus TextFlint perturbations
Analysis of davinci's instruction comprehension and in-context learning via analyzability rate
Findings on the effect of SFT, code training, FeedME and PPO/RLHF on NLU performance

method.summary: Six OpenAI API models were prompted zero-, 1- and 3-shot with three hand-picked prompts per dataset on 21 NLU datasets and their TextFlint-transformed versions. Scores are reported as mean ± an undefined spread; davinci additionally gets an analyzability-rate analysis. Test-set size differs by model.
method.task: Natural language understanding: ABSA, MRC, NER (English and Chinese), NLI, POS (English and Chinese), RE, sentiment classification, semantic matching, Winograd

datasets.name: 21 datasets (SemEval2014-Laptop 331, -Restaurant 492; SQuAD1.1 9868, SQuAD2.0 11491; ACE2005 1312, CoNLL2003 3453, OntoNotes v5 4019, HONOR 1120, MSRANER 4365, OntoNote4NER 4346; MNLI-m 9815, MNLI-mm 9832, SNLI 10000; Daily547 546, WSJ 5461, PKU-SEGPOS 5204; Tacred 15509; IMDB 11257; MRPC 1724, QQP 5000; WSC273 570)
datasets.split: not stated which split; models other than text-davinci-003 and gpt-3.5-turbo use a 100 or 1000 sample subset
datasets.source: 16 of 21 collated by TextFlint; robustness variants from TextFlint
datasets.preprocessing: Labels for RE, NER, POS mapped to phrases in the prompt

other.note: paper speculates a smaller model than text-davinci-003; not stated

inference.samples: Three prompts per dataset per shot setting; run count and meaning of the ± not stated. davinci/code-davinci-002 on 100 items, text-davinci-001/002 on 1000, text-davinci-003/gpt-3.5-turbo on the full set (datasets under 1000 used in full); how the subsets were drawn is not stated
inference.prompting: Zero-shot, 1-shot and 3-shot; three prompts per dataset taken from promptsource or hand-written ('the three best-performing prompts per dataset'); prompts end with 'Answer:' for most tasks; 3-shot adds examples to the 1-shot prompt; selection of few-shot examples not described

parameters.analyzable_rate_threshold: not given; '-' marks non-analyzable rate above it (Table 22)

other.fewshot_example: one fixed example per dataset, reused across the three prompts and, for 3-shot, extended (3-shot prompts are not printed); 1-shot example labels: MNLI-m entailment, MNLI-mm contradiction, SNLI neutral, MRPC Yes, QQP No, WSC yes, IMDB positive
other.format_instruction: For NER, Chinese NER and POS the zero-shot prompts state the output format, while the 1-shot prompts drop that sentence and rely on the example
other.prompt_defects: WSJ 1-shot example labels 'past particle verb' and 'preposition or conjuction', which are not in the candidate list; Tacred options list repeats 'person and state or province of birth'; Table 27 is titled SQuAD1.0 for SQuAD1.1 data

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: ABSA, NLI, POS (English), SC, SM, WSC

metrics.name: Analyzable rate
metrics.definition: share of davinci outputs that can be parsed to an answer; non-analyzable counted wrong

baselines: Comparison among the six models; no fine-tuned baselines
eval.protocol: Original vs TextFlint-transformed ('ori' vs 'trans') subsets for robustness; mean ± undefined spread; no significance test; 'ori' column compared to 'trans' column for robustness

availability.data: TextFlint-based transformed data; datasets public; release not stated

results.claim: Adding the word 'Answer' at the end of a zero-shot MRPC prompt took davinci's analyzable rate from 0 to 100%.

results.claim: Table 22 and the prose disagree on SQuAD1.1 zero-shot: the table gives text-davinci-002 89.01 and text-davinci-001 86.17 above code-davinci-002 83.44, while the text says code-davinci-002 is best by far.
results.note: Text: 'code-davinci-002 shows much better performance than the other four models'. Table 4 ori columns agree with the text (83.58 vs 78.56 and 73.38), Table 22 does not. Table 22 differs from the per-dataset tables elsewhere too (WSJ text-davinci-003 88.45 vs 75.02 in Table 15; MRPC code-davinci-002 73.51 vs 70.00 in Table 19); how Table 22 is derived is not stated.

results.claim: MRPC zero-shot, code-davinci-002, SwapAnt original: 26.00±45.03, a spread wider than the mean.
results.setup: MRPC SwapAnt 'ori' subset (158 samples), zero-shot, code-davinci-002 (100-sample evaluation)
results.note: The ± is never defined. 45.03 is the sample standard deviation (n-1) of 0, 0 and 78, so the mean 26.00 fits three prompt values; the same holds for QQP code-davinci-002 zero-shot SwapAnt ori 32.14±55.67 (Table 20), which fits 0, 0 and 96.43. This is a reviewer inference, not stated. The cell sits under the SwapAnt column group headed '# 158 samples' (NumWord 402, all 1724); code-davinci-002 was run on 100 samples, so 78.00 is probably 78 of 100.

results.claim: SwapAnt causes up to a 61.64% drop in average performance on semantic matching.
results.note: Reviewer arithmetic: 61.64 equals the text-davinci-001 QQP zero-shot SwapAnt drop in points, 75.65 (ori) minus 14.01 (trans), Table 20. The paper does not name the cell, and says 'average performance'.
results.quote:
SwapAnt results in up to a 61.64% drop in average
performance

results.claim: The authors conclude that GPT-series evolution does not give universal improvement across NLU tasks and that robustness did not improve notably.
results.quote: Our findings reveal that the evolution of GPT series models does not necessarily lead to universal improvements across all NLU tasks

results.claim: On IMDB most models do worse in few-shot than zero-shot; authors speculate long inputs hurt.

limits: No run count, decoding settings, temperature or sampling of subsets is stated; the ± is not defined.
Sample sizes differ by model (100 / 1000 / full set), so cross-model comparisons mix sample sizes.
Analyzability threshold never stated; non-analyzable models drop out as '-'.
GPT-4 not tested (API not available); authors concede reduced samples due to API rate limits.
Explanations (RLHF, smaller model, SFT task mix) are speculation; OpenAI model details undocumented.
Models studied are deprecated API models.
Table 22 (the zero-shot summary in Figure 2) does not match the per-dataset tables and its derivation is not stated.
Several prose claims are contradicted by the tables (MRC 3-shot margin, MNLI-m SwapAnt, MRPC code-davinci-002, IMDB 3-shot).
The 3-shot prompts and their examples are not printed; only the 1-shot form is in Appendix B.

terms.definition: Proportion of model outputs that can be parsed as an answer for the task; non-analyzable results are counted as wrong for davinci

figures.caption: The performance of different models in zero-shot scenario.
figures.why: Per-dataset bar chart of all models; missing bars show non-analyzable cases

figures.caption: The analyzability rates of davinci’s answer results in the zero-shot scenario.

problems: Table 22 SQuAD1.1 zero-shot values disagree with the prose and Table 4.
Table 24 SemEval2014-Laptop w/ 'Answer' 87.00 vs Table 23 zero-shot analyzable rate 86.00.
Section 4.1.2 says analyzability drops on most datasets, but Table 24 IMDB (95 -> 94) and Restaurant (14 -> 13) show no gain.
PDF text extraction splits tables across pages; Table 22 rows are interleaved with page numbers.
Table 5 3-shot code-davinci-002 row duplicates Table 4's row cell for cell.
Table 22 values differ from the per-dataset tables, for example WSJ text-davinci-003 88.45 vs 75.02 in Table 15.
Prose claims contradicted by tables: Sec 4.2.2 (ten to twenty points), 4.2.4 (SwapAnt), 4.2.7 (IMDB few-shot), 4.2.8 (MRPC).
